We use the **Moltbook Observatory Archive** on Hugging Face ([dataset card][hf-moltbook-archive]): an incremental
export of the Moltbook Observatory SQLite database, published as date-partitioned Parquet for browsing and
programmatic access. Each observatory table is exposed as a **subset** (configuration) of the same dataset id. We
load **`agents`**, **`posts`**, **`comments`**, and **`submolts`** for agent metadata, post text and scores, comment
text with scores and parent links, and submolt (community) metadata respectively, matching the dataset card.

The archive is derived from periodic snapshots of the **passive** Moltbook Observatory system (observe-only, no
posting); see the live dashboard and upstream code for context ([GitHub][molt-gh], [live instance][molt-live]).

The dataset is published with the **MIT** license.

**Attribution.** Dataset and tooling by **Sushant Gautam** and **Michael A. Riegler** (SimulaMet / Hugging Face
Datasets, 2026), as listed on the dataset page **Contributors** section.

[hf-moltbook-archive]: https://huggingface.co/datasets/SimulaMet/moltbook-observatory-archive
[molt-gh]: https://github.com/kelkalot/moltbook-observatory
[molt-live]: https://moltbook-observatory.sushant.info.np/

## Dataset Acquisition

The [`datasets`][hf-datasets] library from Hugging Face provides **`load_dataset`**, a single entry point that
downloads (or streams) a dataset repository from the Hub, reads the dataset script or Parquet layout, and returns a
**`DatasetDict`** keyed by split names (often just `train`). You pass the **dataset id** (`org/name`), an optional
**subset** when the repo defines multiple configurations (here `agents`, `posts`, `comments`, `submolts`). Results
are converted to **pandas** `DataFrame`s and written to Parquet under `data/` for faster local reuse.

[hf-datasets]: https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/

```{python}
#| label: load-hf
#| echo: true
#| warning: true
#| message: true

import pandas as pd
from datasets import load_dataset
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

from pathlib import Path
from utils import Data


def _to_df(ds) -> pd.DataFrame:
    splits = list(ds.keys())
    if len(splits) == 1:
        return ds[splits[0]].to_pandas()

    return pd.concat([ds[s].to_pandas() for s in splits], ignore_index=True)


def download(name):
    HF_DATASET = "SimulaMet/moltbook-observatory-archive"
    print(f"Downloading {name} from Hugging Face")
    return _to_df(load_dataset(HF_DATASET, name))

original = Data().load('orig')

for d in original.keys():
    if original[d] is None:
        original[d] = download(d)

# TODO: No need to save if we loaded
original.save('orig')

for name in original.keys():
    df = original[name]
    display(Markdown(f"**`{name}`** - `{df.shape}`"))
    display(df.head(2))
```

After initial inspection, we remove columns that are not needed for downstream analysis, cast timestamp-like fields to
Python-friendly datetime types, and standardize indexing across tables.

```{python}
#| label: data-first-pass
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

def cast_datetime_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    possible = ("timestamp", "time", "date", "created", "updated", "seen", "fetched", "dump")
    for col in df.columns:
        s = df[col]
        if not any(x in col for x in possible):
            continue

        df[col] = pd.to_datetime(s, utc=True, errors="coerce").dt.tz_convert(None)


clean = original.copy()
## --- agents   --- 
clean.agents.drop(columns=["avatar_url", "dump_date"], inplace=True)
clean.agents.set_index('id', drop=True, inplace=True)
cast_datetime_columns(clean.agents)

## --- comments --- 
clean.comments.drop(columns=["fetched_at", "dump_date"], inplace=True)
clean.comments.set_index('id', drop=True, inplace=True)
cast_datetime_columns(clean.comments)

## --- posts    --- 
clean.posts.drop(columns=["dump_date"], inplace=True)
clean.posts.set_index('id', drop=True, inplace=True)
cast_datetime_columns(clean.posts)

## --- submolts --- 
clean.submolts.drop(columns=["dump_date"], inplace=True)
clean.submolts.set_index('name', drop=True, inplace=True)
cast_datetime_columns(clean.submolts)
```

#| label: data-describe

```{python}
#| label: data-posts-cleanup
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false


df_clean: pd.DataFrame = clean.posts.copy()
print(f"Posts : {df_clean.shape}")

# Drop Duplicates
df_clean.drop_duplicates(inplace=True)
print(f"After dropping duplicates: {df_clean.shape}")

# Drop short posts
df_clean.dropna(subset=["content"], inplace=True)
print(f"After dropping empty posts: {df_clean.shape}")
df_clean = df_clean[df_clean["content"].str.strip().str.len() >= 10]
print(f"After dropping short posts: {df_clean.shape}")
```

```{python}
#| label: data-posts-rename
#| message: false

# For compatibility with downstream sections
df_clean.rename(
    columns={
    "agent_name": "agent",
    "content": "post",
    "created_at": "timestamp",
    "submolt": "submolt"
}, inplace=True)
```

```{python}
#| label: save

clean.posts=df_clean
clean.save('clean')
```
